results.name: last_digit_match_effect
results.description: Among non-member targets of sets with 2+ examples, yes rate when the target shares the final digit of all examples minus yes rate otherwise; observed above null means people generalise "ends in d" more than the model, below means less.
results.code:
# name: last_digit_match_effect
# description: Among non-member targets of sets with 2+ examples, yes rate when the target shares the final digit of all examples minus yes rate otherwise; observed above null means people generalise "ends in d" more than the model, below means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float)
    k = s.notna().sum(axis=1).values
    member = s.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1).values
    match = ((s % 10).eq(t % 10, axis=0) | s.isna()).all(axis=1).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    base = (k >= 2) & ~member
    a, b = base & match, base & ~match
    if not a.any() or not b.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: cross_set_lag1_agreement
results.description: Proportion of consecutive trials (trial_index increases by 1, in row order) with different sets that receive the same response; observed above null means responses carry over between trials (participant bias/stickiness) that the independent-trial model lacks.

results.name: proximity_gradient_nonmembers
results.description: Among non-member targets, yes rate for targets within 3 of the nearest example minus yes rate for targets more than 20 away; observed below null means the model predicts a steeper similarity/distance gradient than people show.
results.code:
# name: proximity_gradient_nonmembers
# description: Among non-member targets, yes rate for targets within 3 of the nearest example minus yes rate for targets more than 20 away; observed below null means the model predicts a steeper similarity/distance gradient than people show.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float)
    dist = s.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    near = (dist > 0) & (dist <= 3)
    far = dist > 20
    a = r[near].mean() if near.any() else 0.0
    b = r[far].mean() if far.any() else 0.0
    return float(a - b)

results.name: between_set_rate_dispersion
results.description: Standard deviation across sets (with at least 20 trials) of the per-set yes rate; observed above null means people's overall willingness to say yes varies between sets more than the model's concept posterior produces.

results.name: member_target_yes_rate
results.description: Yes rate on trials whose target is one of the shown examples; observed below null means the model over-predicts endorsement of the examples themselves (too reliable), above means it under-predicts.

results.name: threshold_extension_asymmetry
results.description: For sets whose examples all lie in one half (all >=50 or all <=50), yes rate for out-of-range targets on the side toward the nearer end of the number line (above max for high sets, below min for low sets) minus yes rate on the opposite side; observed below null means the model over-predicts one-sided threshold extension.
results.code:
# name: threshold_extension_asymmetry
# description: For sets whose examples all lie in one half (all >=50 or all <=50), yes rate for out-of-range targets on the side toward the nearer end of the number line (above max for high sets, below min for low sets) minus yes rate on the opposite side; observed below null means the model over-predicts one-sided threshold extension.
def test_statistic(df):
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).astype(float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).values
    mn = s.min(axis=1).values
    mx = s.max(axis=1).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    hi = mn >= 50
    lo = (mx <= 50) & ~hi
    toward = (hi & (t > mx)) | (lo & (t < mn))
    away = (hi & (t < mn)) | (lo & (t > mx))
    if not toward.any() or not away.any():
        return 0.0
    return float(r[toward].mean() - r[away].mean())

results.name: set_size_yes_slope
results.description: Yes rate on non-member targets for 1-example sets minus that for 4-example sets; observed below null means the model's size principle over-predicts how much extra examples narrow generalisation, above means it under-predicts.

def test_statistic(df):

results.name: parity_match_effect
results.description: Among non-member targets of sets with 2+ examples, yes rate when the target shares the parity of all examples minus yes rate when it does not; observed below null means the model over-weights odd/even-style rules relative to people.

# description: Among non-member targets of sets with 2+ examples, yes rate when the target shares the parity of all examples minus yes rate when it does not; observed below null means the model over-weights odd/even-style rules relative to people.
